podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Connection to U2 Management
podcast.body: Barry Devlin, the bassist and vocalist for Horslips, recommended a young band named U2 to his friend Paul McGinnis, who was a big Horslips fan. This recommendation led to Paul McGinnis becoming U2's manager. "One thing that you should know about horse-lips is that bassist and vocalist Barry Devlin recommended a young band to his friend, who was a very big horse-lips fan, and that friend's name was Paul McGinnis. And that's how Paul McGinnis became the manager of U2."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Major Irish International Success
podcast.body: This band achieved significant success outside of Ireland without needing to leave their home country first, a notable accomplishment for an Irish band at the time. "They were also the first major Irish band to have success outside of Ireland without having to leave the country first."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation and Mission
podcast.body: Horslips was formed in Dublin in 1970 with the specific goal of updating traditional Irish and Celtic folk music. They are recognized as the first group to be labeled "Celtic rock" and are considered the founding fathers of the genre. "They were formed in Dublin in 1970 and were on a mission to update traditional Irish and Celtic folk music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Impact on Irish Music Revival
podcast.body: Along with Thin Lizzy, Horslips faced criticism from traditionalists in Ireland but played a crucial role in revitalizing interest in traditional Irish music. "Both Thin Lizzy and Horse-lips took a lot of abuse from the musical traditionalists of Ireland, but both contributed greatly to a revival of interest in traditional Irish music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Managerial Learning for Paul McGuinness
podcast.body: Irish folk rock band Horslips were quite successful in Ireland, and their manager was a friend of Paul McGuinness. By "hanging around with them," McGuinness gained valuable insights and learned several aspects of being a manager, which later informed his own career.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Impact on Irish Music Revival
xref.body: Thin Lizzy, along with Horslips, faced considerable criticism from musical traditionalists in Ireland, yet they made significant contributions to a revival of interest in traditional Irish music. "Both Thin Lizzy and Horse-lips took a lot of abuse from the musical traditionalists of Ireland, but both contributed greatly to a revival of interest in traditional Irish music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influences and Style
xref.body: The band drew inspiration from the British metal band Skyclad and the folk stylings of Horslips, then incorporated death metal elements into their sound. This fusion created a sound described as "the darkest, heaviest, drinkingest pub music you've ever heard." "They were formed in Dublin in 1992, taking cues not only from a British metal band called Skyclad, but also the folk styleings of horse-lips. Then they added a little death metal to the mix, because you know, why not. What does that even sound like? Well, like the darkest, heaviest, drinkingest pub music you've ever heard."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Manager of U2
xref.body: Paul McGinnis became the manager of U2 after receiving a recommendation from Barry Devlin, bassist and vocalist of Horslips, who knew McGinnis was a big fan of Horslips. "And that's how Paul McGinnis became the manager of U2."
